Welcome To Manor Primary School
We are unique in that we are a five form entry Infant school on the Leftley Estate at Sandringham Road in Barking and a three form entry Primary school set in a modern building on Longbridge Road in Dagenham.
Our vision is to provide all our children with a challenging, engaging and safe environment, which promotes a lifelong love of learning. This ethos is evident in all we do.
We offer a thoughtful sequential curriculum, which challenges the children to be creative and to become resilient and learn the skills they will need for their future lives. Our Values Education programme promotes harmony, honesty and integrity, whilst our exciting, creative curriculum harnesses and reflects our vibrant community of London.
We take pride in all we do and welcome visitors to come and see school life in action.
History of Manor Primary School
Manor Infant School opened on Sandringham Road in 1935 to serve a rapidly growing population in East London. It has since gone from strength to strength and has now expanded to become a 5-form entry school which continues to provide high quality education for all its children.
The Manor Longbridge site opened in September 2011 again to serve the rapid population growth in East London. It is a 3-form entry Primary School which is housed in a modern building.

Our Remote Education
At Manor Primary School, we aim to provide all our children with a challenging, engaging safe environment which promotes a lifelong love of learning, be that at school or remotely.
At Manor Primary School we use the following to support learning:
Purple Mash is used as our main source of contact. Overtime, as the children become more familiar with it, they will be able to contact their class teacher via an online blog. Regular work is set by their class teacher as ‘2dos’ for the children to access and consolidate their learning.
In addition, we use MyMaths to support the teaching of maths. Here you will find homework that has been set to target your child’s learning, as well as MyMaths lessons that your child can choose to do as revision for any topics they may be unsure of.
Other useful websites that we recommend:
BBC Bitesize Maths Zone Education City BBC Super Movers
Full or Partial Lockdown:
Communication between home and school is pivotal for the success of your child. Each Year Group have a dedicated email that will be checked regularly in the event of a full or partial lockdown. Your child’s class teacher will contact your child via the phone to ensure they are confident with any work that has been provided and their login details.

Our Role as a School
The school will be open to all pupils.
The school will provide children with login information and educate them on how to access online materials. For example, Purple Mash.

If a ‘bubble’ has to be sent home, or there is an official lockdown, the school will provide daily lessons and activities for children that will be targeted appropriately.

Our curriculum is sequenced purposefully, with careful attention given to what pupils should learn in each subject during their time at school with us. Knowledge and skills are progressively organised so that pupils build on what they already know, ensuring that they are appropriately challenged and have a secure understanding of their learning.
Our curriculum is enriched with many exciting experiences and opportunities, broadening pupils’ horizons and encouraging resilience and enquiry into the unknown. This rich cultural capital, together with our Values Education and British Values, ensures that our pupils become personally successful and independent thinkers, ready for their lifelong learning journey.
Our curriculum ensures that content is explicitly taught, with frequent and regular opportunities for retrieval of previously learned material and opportunities to practise skills. We use a variety of resources, including Cornerstones, to create a curriculum that matches the interests and needs of our children.
Subject-specific vocabulary is explicitly taught to ensure depth of understanding, improved comprehension skills, and the ability to think about and understand the world. Our pupils are provided with a wide range of engaging, challenging, and varied texts that help them access a rich depth of curriculum knowledge. Pupils are encouraged to read prolifically, and we aim to inspire a lifelong love of reading in all our children and families.
We promote an awareness and understanding of pupils’ own learning so that they may assess their progress and take part in setting targets for continued attainment in the future. The future is uncertain, but what is certain is that respect for others will help our children make the most of the skills and knowledge that our school aims to impart.

pageCache.pageTitle: Clubs and Activities – Manor Primary School
pageCache.text:
We offer a wide range of extra-curricular activities. Recent clubs include: football, dance, multisports, basketball, tag rugby, music, art, design and technology, drama, judo, and more.
These are available during lunch time or after school. The clubs enable children to learn and consolidate new skills in a fun environment.
There is a charge for our clubs to cover the running costs. Some of our clubs are run by third parties, including Premier Education. Where this is the case, families wishing to access the clubs will be directed to the third party’s website to book directly.
We also offer a range of academic booster clubs that are offered to specific children at different points throughout the year. If the available sessions are appropriate for your child, you will receive a personal invitation.
There is not a cost associated with these clubs.
We have a variety of after school clubs, these include football, cooking, art, music, design and technology and other sports. These dates are always subject to change.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND and Inclusion – Manor Primary School
pageCache.text:
(SEND stands for Special Educational Needs and Disability)
The school policy for Special Educational Needs (SEN) is one of integration and equal opportunity so that all pupils have access to the National Curriculum and are encouraged to achieve to their full potential.
The school follows the DCSF guidelines as stated in the Code of Practice for SEN 2014. If our assessments show that a child may have a learning difficulty a range of strategies are used that make full use of classroom and school resources. This level of support is called SEN Support.
Individual targets are introduced and monitored carefully.
Staff are able to request support from outside services when appropriate.
Should a child continue to demonstrate significant cause for concern a request for an Education and Health Care Plan can be made to the LA. If an EHC Plan is issued the LA is responsible for monitoring and reviewing the provision in liaison with the school.
At each stage the child’s progress is reviewed regularly.
Parents are informed and consulted at each of the stages and their views are essential in providing a strong partnership between home and school. Each new member is given an induction session outlining the school’s SEN policy, procedures and provision.
There is also close consultation with Manor Junior School to ensure continuity and progression with supporting individual children in the transfer between the Infant and Junior Schools.
Disability Equality Scheme
The school has responded to the Disability Discrimination Act (DDA) 2005 by preparing a Disability Equality Scheme (DES). The implementation and impact of the scheme is monitored by the Governors.
There is also an Action Plan relating to the DES which runs alongside a Disability Access Plan. These are both reviewed on a yearly basis and form part of the School Development Plan.

pageCache.pageTitle: Additional Resource Provision – Manor Primary School
pageCache.text:
At Manor Primary (Longbridge site), we have an Additional Resource Provision (ARP) which caters for twelve pupils with a diagnosis of autism (ASC). All of our pupils have an Education Health Care Plan (EHCP) and pupils are allocated spaces in the ARP through the Local Authority SEND (Special Education Needs and Disability) Panel and not by the school or via school admissions.
Teaching and learning
The ARP is a highly structured environment where pupils have access to a curriculum aimed to meet their individual needs and abilities, using targets acquired from our rigorous assessments.
Our ARP has three separate curriculum pathways: pre-formal (sensory based/engagement); semi-formal explorers and semi-formal challengers; and the formal learners (mainstream). These cater for the needs of all pupils in similar ways.
Each curriculum pathway is well thought of and includes individual targets, which ensure that, a range of approaches and interventions are used to support and enhance the learning experiences for all pupils.
The schedule for the day ensures pupils’ participation in group activities, aimed at developing communication skills and turn-taking skills, and improving attention.
The ARP is well staffed. There are two teachers and four teaching assistants. All staff engage in specialist and ongoing training related to autism teaching and learning. Other professionals who are available to support staff and pupils include an Autism Adviser, a Speech and Language Therapist and an Educational Psychologist.
All pupils are on roll in a year group in the mainstream, appropriate to their age. Where possible, integration is planned for on an individual basis and this is dependent on a number of factors. These centre on the needs and interests of the individual pupil at that time. Some of the activities the children join in, in the mainstream include, educational visits, PE and break times.
This is based on the pupils’ sensory, emotional and regulatory needs. They have support from of a member of staff from the ARP for this integration.
Educational visits and Wider Curriculum experiences
Our pupils have the opportunity to go on educational visits each academic year. These visits have included sensory experiences such as soft play, adventure and nature play experiences as well as swimming lessons.
